_comment: Locked, global, production design system. Every value here applies to every post identically. Nothing in this file is derived from an image, computed automatically, or sampled from a photo — it is fixed by hand and stays fixed. Per-post layout (crop, text position, sizes) lives in config/layouts.json, never here.

canvas._note: Each master's own dimensions are preserved exactly. This is only a sanity check that a master is still close to the target aspect ratio — never a resize/crop target. Swap [4, 5] for whatever ratio your platform wants (e.g. [1, 1] for square, [9, 16] for a Story).

_minEdgePadding_note: The one number that decides 'does this fit' everywhere in the system. Pick it based on your canvas size and smallest planned font — see references/templates.md.
_fonts_note: Use the FULL-coverage release of each font (not a hand-trimmed Latin-only subset) if you will ever localize into a language with diacritics — see references/localization.md. Two font roles is the minimum (a display headline face + a workhorse body/UI face for support text and the wordmark); a third face for the wordmark is fine if your brand uses one.
_colors_note: Replace with your brand's real values — pull them from an existing design token file if one exists (a live site's CSS custom properties, a brand guide) rather than inventing new ones. 'accent' is the one color used to highlight a single headline line (see copy.json's accentLineIndex); 'panelBackground' is the solid color behind TEMPLATE_SIDE's panel and TEMPLATE_BOTTOM's band.
_locked_note: Not read by any code — a checklist for a human (or a reviewing Claude) to confirm the finished system still honors the constraints it was built under. Delete flags that don't apply to your brief; don't add automation that would falsify one of these while it's still listed true.

templates._comment: 3 deterministic, reusable templates. The canvas is always the MASTER's own width/height (never resized/upscaled) — a real photo set often has more than one native size, so TEMPLATE_SIDE/TEMPLATE_BOTTOM panel geometry is stored as a RATIO of the master's own dimensions, not a fixed pixel size. A post's layout entry sets `template: "A"|"B"|"C"` and, for A/C, `photoCrop` (the region extracted from the master, in the MASTER's own pixel coordinates) — its width/height must exactly equal that master's own computed panel size (canvasWidth*photoPanelWidthRatio for A, canvasHeight*photoBandHeightRatio for C, each rounded) so no scaling is ever needed. Master files are never touched; only this derived, in-memory crop is composited onto a flat panelBackground canvas. See references/templates.md for when to choose which and how to pick the ratios for your own layout.

A._description: TEMPLATE_SIDE — a solid panel of brand color on one side, the photo (cropped to fill) on the other. Text never touches the photo at all.

B._description: TEMPLATE_FULL — text overlaid directly on the full photo. Only for a photo with genuinely large, clean negative space that the text will never come near a face/hands/product on; never forced onto a busy photo just because a batch 'needs variety'.

C._description: TEMPLATE_BOTTOM — the photo (cropped to fill) on top, a solid band of brand color below it. Text never touches the photo at all.
